requirements.text: Put a frog in the toilet
requirements.source_phrase: Put a frog in the toilet

outcomes.description: Add a frog inside the toilet.
outcomes.target: A frog is visibly placed within the toilet bowl.
outcomes.reference: The toilet in the input image.

nodes.question: Is a frog visibly present inside the toilet bowl?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image clearly shows a frog within the toilet bowl; fail if the bowl is visible and no frog is inside it; unknown if the bowl or its contents cannot be assessed reliably.
nodes.binding: Assess the frog’s placement relative to the toilet bowl in the image, using the toilet in the input image as the reference. A frog elsewhere does not satisfy this check.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show the requested frog placement at the original toilet, and is there visible evidence that the requested placement is incomplete?
nodes.criteria: Pass if visible evidence shows a frog placed in or on the original toilet in a way that constitutes progress toward putting a frog in the toilet; fail only if the toilet is assessable and there is no visible frog placement at it; unknown if visibility is insufficient. Report any clearly visible additional frogs elsewhere as evidence, but do not treat their presence alone as negating the requested placement.
nodes.binding: Assess visible frog placement relative to the toilet in the input image. This check reports evidence of progress and possible incompleteness; it does not decide overall fulfillment. Do not impose a requirement that extra frogs be absent.

nodes.question: Is a frog visibly placed inside the toilet bowl?
nodes.criteria: For R1, complete if the supports establish that at least one frog is visibly placed in or on the original toilet in a way that fulfills “Put a frog in the toilet,” and there is no supported evidence that the requested placement itself remains incomplete. Partial if the supports establish some requested frog placement at the toilet but also establish that the requested placement is incomplete; additional frogs elsewhere alone do not make the requested change incomplete. Absent if the supports establish no requested frog placement or progress at the toilet. Unknown if necessary evidence is insufficient or unresolved; do not infer completion, partial progress, or absence from uncertainty. Unrelated edits are not progress.
nodes.binding: Target: A frog is visibly placed within the toilet bowl.. Reference: The toilet in the input image..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The fulfillment rule is too permissive: it treats a frog placed “in or on” the original toilet as complete, although the request and target require a frog inside the toilet bowl. Support s2 also treats placement “in or on” the toilet as progress, so a frog merely on the toilet could be reported as progress despite not satisfying the requested spatial relation. The readout therefore cannot faithfully distinguish the requested placement from a weaker one."}

parsed.reason: The fulfillment rule is too permissive: it treats a frog placed “in or on” the original toilet as complete, although the request and target require a frog inside the toilet bowl. Support s2 also treats placement “in or on” the toilet as progress, so a frog merely on the toilet could be reported as progress despite not satisfying the requested spatial relation. The readout therefore cannot faithfully distinguish the requested placement from a weaker one.
